original_question: Describe the structure of Jones-Wenzl-type projectors inside the Brauer algebra that arises from adding virtual crossings to the Temperley-Lieb algebra, and determine whether that setting supports a useful algebraic generalization of classical recoupling theory.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact algebraic setting in the paper: adding virtual crossings to the Temperley–Lieb algebra, viewing the result as the Brauer algebra, asking about the Jones–Wenzl projectors there, and asking whether this yields a useful generalization of classical recoupling theory. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
missing_details: The paper says Jones–Wenzl projectors, not “Jones–Wenzl-type projectors,” so the draft is slightly less exact than the paper’s wording. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should name the intermediate object “Virtual Temperley–Lieb Algebra,” since the paper phrases the Brauer-algebra identification through that terminology. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The paper specifies the Brauer algebra here as the algebra of all connections from n points to n points; the draft omits this n-point/n-point description. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The paper leaves n implicit as a size/strand parameter; a stand-alone research question should state whether n is fixed or whether the question is posed for each n. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The paper does not specify the ground ring, parameter choices, or coefficient field for the Temperley–Lieb/Brauer setting, so those data remain implicit rather than fully formalized. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The paper does not formalize what “the structure of the projectors” should mean—e.g. existence, uniqueness, recursion, basis expansion, idempotency relations, or annihilation properties—so a precise stand-alone version must keep this wording broad without pretending the paper supplied sharper algebraic criteria. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

Likewise, the paper does not define what counts as a “useful algebraic generalization” of classical recoupling theory, so that usefulness criterion must remain intentionally open-ended if the rewrite is to stay paper-faithful. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
refined_question: For the Brauer algebra B_n obtained by adjoining virtual crossings to the Temperley–Lieb algebra—equivalently, the paper’s “Virtual Temperley–Lieb Algebra,” described as the algebra of all connections from n points to n points—determine the structure of the Jones–Wenzl projectors when placed in B_n, and decide whether this Brauer-algebra setting admits a useful algebraic generalization of the classical Temperley–Lieb recoupling theory. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
justification: This draft is targeting the paper’s Problem 14 almost verbatim. Section 8.1 explicitly asks about placing Jones–Wenzl projectors in the Brauer algebra obtained by adding virtual crossings to the Temperley–Lieb algebra and asks whether a useful algebraic generalization of classical recoupling theory can be formulated. Section 2.1 supplies the paper’s background notion of adding virtual crossings, and refs. [120] and [122] are the paper’s immediate internal pointers for classical Temperley–Lieb recoupling theory and Temperley–Lieb algebra background. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
